title: Five-table sales warehouse and versioned consumer scope
context: The customers-orders/v1 consumer acknowledged mixed archive batches while ignoring three captured sales tables. A broader consumer must revisit those batches without resetting archive state or overwriting the first consumer checkpoints.

decision.schema: Additive migration 002; migration 001 remains byte-for-byte unchanged.
decision.checkpoints: Keep ops.archive_batches as first-seen provenance; ops.consumer_batches acknowledges each (consumer_version,batch_id). Seed the v1 acknowledgments, revalidate all five table prefixes and _mixed for v2, deduplicate using unchanged source-event identities.
decision.contract: Owner-controlled ops.consumer_contracts fixes table scope, source instance, snapshot generation/LSN, archive prefix and layout. Routine polling refuses drift.
decision.model: Five source-scoped hubs, six relationship links, five append-only event satellites and current pointers. Parent hubs can be inferred before parent events. Historical links do not imply a current relationship.
decision.invoice_relationships: Keep sold-to CustomerID and BillToCustomerID as separate roles. OrderID is optional. InvoiceLines has no direct OrderLineID: do not infer a line mapping from StockItemID.
decision.query_grains: order_details has one row per current order line; invoice_details one row per current invoice line; invoice_summary aggregates lines at invoice grain before joining.
decision.money: Preserve source decimal values; typed query columns use PostgreSQL numeric; reconciliation decodes JSON numbers as Decimal. Credit notes preserve signed source amounts without automatic inversion.
decision.computed_columns: Rebuild ConfirmedDeliveryTime and ConfirmedReceivedBy from ReturnedDeliveryData in the invoice query view, because SQL Server CDC change tables return NULL for computed columns. Keep raw event images unchanged. The delivery-time helper supports the ISO form in this fixture and returns text to preserve seven fractional digits; it is not a general T-SQL conversion engine.
decision.validation: Stream source NDJSON and target server-side cursors to bound memory. Compare full primary-key sets, explicit business projections, six parent references, view grains and invoice totals. Source scans share one SERIALIZABLE transaction during a quiet lab validation window.
decision.runtime: No additional permanent service. Watch worker: 512 MiB / 0.75 CPU. One-off backfill: 768 MiB / 1.5 CPU. Retain the existing 4-vCPU/12-GiB VM.
decision.source_probe_session: Synthetic DML sets ANSI_NULLS, ANSI_PADDING, ANSI_WARNINGS, ARITHABORT, CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL and QUOTED_IDENTIFIER ON, with NUMERIC_ROUNDABORT OFF, as required by SQL Server indexed expressions/filtered indexes. No database-wide setting is changed.

rollback: Retain image decom-warehouse-loader:1, original source tar and protected pre-v2 logical backup in /srv/decom-sqlserver/releases/warehouse-sales-v2-20261028.
To pause an incident, stop only the warehouse loader; preserve SQL Server capture and SeaweedFS archives.

A full rollback restores the pre-v2 dump into a separate database, checks it with the original v1 source/image, then switches consumers deliberately. Do not drop the expanded warehouse or blindly run v1 against expanded current views.
Replay later raw archives after recovery. Never reset Debezium offsets, delete prior archive generations or delete old consumer acknowledgments.
limits: The five captured tables are not the whole SQL Server database. Stored procedures, jobs, ownership and application dependencies remain a separate workstream.
Spatial and audit columns remain outside the explicit business reconciliation projection.
SERIALIZABLE source scans can block writes; independent source/target snapshots are not a general online cutover protocol.
Atomicity is per archived batch. Parent/child changes spanning batches can be temporarily inconsistent.
Discovery lists manifest keys in memory; a production discovery catalog and compaction require separate capacity work.

The datetime helper covers the documented ISO input contract only; scalar length follows PostgreSQL character counting and is not proven equivalent to SQL Server UTF-16 limits for supplementary Unicode characters.
Same-VM logical backup/restore reuses existing cluster roles; no off-VM disaster recovery or high availability is claimed.
No contiguous coverage watermark or cleanup authorization is produced. SQL CDC cleanup stays disabled.
